allWorkPackages.subject: Analytics - Responsiveness (ketanggapan) section - Inverted Agent Attribution in RLT Average Metric Aggregation
allWorkPackages.description:
# 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary The Resolution/Response Lead Time (RLT) Average metric displays inverted data counts in the top summary section of the Analytics module. An inactive agent who sent zero messages receives a positive RLT Average count, while an active agent who handled the customer chat registers a zero count. This issue occurs on the Analytics module's Responsiveness summary section. It is important because it completely reverses performance tracking, crediting passive users while penalizing active team members, which severely undermines data accuracy and team evaluation. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Prepare 1 SPV account and 2 Agent accounts (Agent A and Agent B). 2. Start a new customer conversation with no initial assignee. 3. Assign both Agent A and Agent B to the conversation via SPV account. 4. Send response messages to the customer exclusively using **Agent A**. 5. Do **not** send any messages using **Agent B**. 6. Close and resolve the conversation using the SPV account. 7. Open the **Analytics Module** > **Responsiveness** section. 8. Filter the top summary stat cards by **Agent A** and observe the RLT Average count. 9. Filter the top summary stat cards by **Agent B** and observe the RLT Average count. ## Actual Result * Agent B (inactive agent) receives a non-zero RLT Average count in the top summary section. * Agent A (active agent) receives a zero count (`0`) for RLT Average despite actively sending responses. ## Expected Result * RLT Average counts must strictly map to the agent who actively logged response or resolution events. * Agent A must receive the calculated RLT Average count. * Agent B must register a zero count (`0`) due to zero contribution. ## Impact ## Evidence Screenshot ##### Only Agent A who have the message in that conversation

##### Agent A average statistics (The Average respons lead time is empty)
##### ##### Agent B average statistics (The average response lead time is have a vallue, even this agent do nothing

Initial Observation * Applying the Agent A filter returns `0` in the top summary RLT Average count card. * Applying the Agent B filter returns a calculated average count for RLT in the top summary card. * Message logs confirm Agent A authored all outgoing customer messages while Agent B authored none. ## Possible Root Cause _(Optional)_ Possible affected areas: * Backend * Database > The aggregation query for top summary RLT metrics appears to map resolution/lead time events to the conversation's initial assignee or secondary member array, while incorrectly omitting or filtering out the active message author ID. ## Recommendation _(Optional)_ 1. Refactor the RLT aggregation logic to target event log timestamps linked explicitly to `message.sender_id` or `ticket_events.actor_id`. 2. Ensure filtering by agent ID checks for active event logs rather than static assignment parameters. 3. Add backend integration tests covering multi-assignee scenarios to verify RLT calculations. ## Additional Notes * This anomaly forms part of a broader metric mapping issue across the Analytics module where conversation state (`assignee_id`) is favored over user action logs (`sender_id`).

allWorkPackages.subject: Analytics - Responsiveness (Ketanggapan) section - FRT Detail View Queries Initial Assignee ID Instead of First Message Sender
allWorkPackages.description:
# 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary The First Response Time (FRT) metric details display incorrect agent attribution in the stat card view. When inspecting an FRT record for a conversation, the system labels the first assigned member as the responder instead of attributing the response to the agent who actually sent the initial outgoing message. This bug occurs on the Conversation module's detailed stat card view. It directly distorts agent performance auditing, creates misleading audit trails for response times, and corrupts the integrity of individual agent reporting. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Assign an incoming customer conversation to Agent B (Agent B becomes the initial assignee). 2. Have Agent A (a different agent) send the first outgoing reply message to the customer. 3. Open the _Analytics_ module, section _Responsiveness_ (Ketanggapan) and locate the FRT stat card. 4. Click on the FRT stat card to view the detailed agent attribution breakdown for that conversation. ## Actual Result * The FRT detail view labels Agent B (the initial assignee) as the agent responsible for the first response. * Agent A is not attributed as the first responder despite sending the initial message. * The FRT calculation reflects the assigned user's ID rather than the actual message sender's ID. ## Expected Result * The FRT detail view must display Agent A as the first responder. * The system should dynamically attribute FRT to the agent who sent the first outgoing message. * Initial assignment changes must not overwrite or determine first responder attribution. ## Impact ## Evidence Screenshot Agent A is the agent who response first But the label agent who first respons is agent B on the detail FRT
Initial Observation * FRT stat card detail popover opens successfully. * The label displayed in the detail record references the conversation's initial `assignee_id`. * Outgoing message sender payload contains the correct active responder ID, but it is ignored by the FRT detail view query. ## Possible Root Cause _(Optional)_ Possible affected areas: * Backend * Database > The database query backing the FRT detail view retrieves the initial `assignee_id` field from the conversation entity rather than querying the author ID of the first outgoing message record. ## Recommendation _(Optional)_ 1. Update the backend SQL query/aggregation logic for FRT stat cards to join with the messages table and filter by `created_at ASC` where `sender_type = 'agent'`. 2. Map the FRT label to `message.sender_id` instead of `conversation.assignee_id`.

allWorkPackages.subject: Analytics - Responsiveness (Ketanggapan) section - Cross-Agent SLA Synchronization Leak Across Multi-Assignee Conversations
allWorkPackages.description: # 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary SLA metrics in the "Dalam SLA" and "Melebihi SLA" section are calculated based on overall conversation data rather than individual agent actions. If Agent A actively handles a conversation while Agent B is merely assigned but inactive, Agent B's personal SLA automatically syncs with Agent A's activity. This may be important because it was linked with the data accuracy, especially on _Analytics_ module, the data must be accurate. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Get ready using 1 SPV account and 2 Agent accounts (Agent A & Agent B). 2. Create a new customer chat (or close current active conversation and re-initiate from customer side). 3. Ensure the conversation has no assigned agent (assignee field must be empty). 4. From the SPV POV, assign both Agent A and Agent B to the conversation. 5. Reply to the customer chat using **Agent A**. 6. Do **not** send any messages using **Agent B**. 7. Close the conversation using the SPV account. 8. Navigate to **Analytics Module** > **Responsiveness** section. 9. Locate the SLA breakdown UI (_"Dalam SLA"_ / _"Melebihi SLA"_). 10. Apply filter for **Agent A**. 11. Observe the stat count and click the breakdown UI to view detail data. Record the count. 12. Apply filter for **Agent B**. 13. Observe, record, and compare the data between Agent A and Agent B. ## Actual Result * Agent B (inactive agent with zero message contributions) receives identical SLA metric counts and status as Agent A. ## Expected Result * SLA calculations must be isolated per agent based on their actual logged actions within a conversation, preventing inactive assignees from inheriting SLA status from active agents. ## Impact ## Evidence Screenshot _Agent A data **(The active agent, this agent active on the conversation)**:_ _Agent B data **(The inactive agent, no message activity contributed)**:_ ## Initial Observation * Filtering responsiveness analytics by Agent A displays SLA records for the target conversation. * Filtering responsiveness analytics by Agent B displays identical SLA records for the target conversation despite zero sent messages by Agent B. * Backend analytics query aggregates SLA compliance by matching `conversation_members.user_id` or `conversation.assignee_id` against the conversation's global SLA status without checking message/event authorship. ## Possible Root Cause _(Optional)_ Possible affected areas: * Backend * Database The analytical SLA aggregation query groups metrics by joining `conversations` directly to assigned users (`assignee_id` or `conversation_members`) and evaluating conversation-level completion timestamps. It lacks a check against message/event logs (`messages.sender_id` or `activity_logs.actor_id`) to verify whether an assigned agent actively participated in resolving the ticket. ## Recommendation _(Optional)_ 1. **Refactor Backend Metric Query:** Update the SLA aggregation logic in the Analytics service to only evaluate conversations where the targeted `agent_id` has at least one logged outgoing message or qualifying SLA action (`sender_type = 'agent'` AND `sender_id = target_agent_id`). 2. **Implement Event-Driven SLA Logs:** Store SLA metrics in an explicit per-agent event table (e.g., `agent_sla_logs`) written when an agent performs a qualifying interaction, rather than computing raw conversation-level metrics on the fly across all assignees. 3. **Handle Multi-Agent Split Metrics:** Define business rules for multi-assignee tickets (e.g., attribute SLA compliance only to the agent who closed/resolved the conversation or sent the final resolving message).

allWorkPackages.subject: Analytics UI/UX-Polish  - Unformatted Floating-Point Numbers in Chart Hover Tooltips
allWorkPackages.description: # UI/UX Polish Collection > This document collects minor UI, UX, interaction, and visual polish observations found during exploratory testing of the Analytics Dashboard. > > These observations are **not critical functional bugs**, but addressing them can improve consistency, readability, and the overall product experience. # Overview # Observation 001 ## Title Chart tooltip displays raw percentage with excessive decimal places ### Screenshot [](https://project.ordo.co.id/api/v3/attachments/659/content) ### Observation When hovering over data bars in the **Tiket (Ticket Analytics)** chart, the tooltip renders the raw calculation output without formatting. The value is shown with up to 15 decimal places (for example, `34.146341463414636%`). The raw division result is rendered directly. No rounding or string formatting is applied before display. The same pattern was observed in **Ketanggapan (Responsiveness Analytics)** for percentage based tooltips when the underlying value is a fraction. ### Expected Behavior Percentage values in tooltips should be rounded to a consistent precision. Recommended presentation is 1 or 2 decimal places with a percent sign (for example, `34.15%` or `34.1%`). The dashboard should use a single shared formatter for all percentage tooltips so the precision is consistent across charts. ### Notes This is a frontend presentation issue. Data correctness is not affected. Only the formatted display in the tooltip needs adjustment. # Observation 002 ## Title Chart tooltip displays raw duration with IEEE 754 floating point artifact ### Screenshot [](https://project.ordo.co.id/api/v3/attachments/661/content) ### Observation When hovering over data bars in the **Ketanggapan (Responsiveness Analytics)** chart, the duration tooltip shows a raw floating point number (for example, `412575.24439999997 mins`). The value contains a JavaScript IEEE 754 precision artifact (`.24439999997`). No rounding, thousand separator, or duration conversion is applied. The tooltip renders the direct numeric result from the calculation. ### Expected Behavior Duration values should be presented in a clean and readable format. Two acceptable options: 1. Rounded integer with thousand separators (for example, `412,575 mins`) 2. Human readable duration conversion (for example, `286 days 12 hrs`) if Product prefers a friendlier unit Either option removes the floating point artifact and reduces visual clutter. The formatter should be reused for all duration tooltips. ### Notes Same root cause as Observation 001. Missing formatter callback in the chart tooltip component. The underlying duration value is correct. Only presentation needs formatting. _**See other hover tooltip on info chart, the chart with mins was have the same bug**_ # Summary # General Notes Both observations share the same root cause. The chart tooltip component renders raw numeric outputs without a formatting layer. Possible affected area: * Frontend Chart Tooltip Component Recommended verification for engineering: 1. Verify tooltip formatter callback is applied to all chart datasets in Tiket and Ketanggapan modules 2. Centralize formatting in a shared utility so percentage and duration use one consistent rule Example utility for reference: ```ts // 1. Percentage Rounding Fix const formatPercentage = (val: number): string => `${val.toFixed(2)}%`; // 2. Duration / Large Number Formatting Fix const formatDuration = (val: number): string => `${Math.round(val).toLocaleString()} mins`; ``` This collection is considered **UI/UX polish**. It does not block functionality and does not require a separate functional bug ticket in `BugErrorReport/report/`. It should be scheduled as a visual polish improvement for the Analytics Dashboard. Evidence images are stored in `./images/` alongside this document.

allWorkPackages.subject: Global Search Suggestion - Search typo tolerance was not working in production version
allWorkPackages.description: # 🐞 Bug Report — Global Search Typo Tolerance (Fuzzy maxEdits: 1) Not Working on Production ## Summary Global Search suggestion on **dev-v2** applies a 1-character typo tolerance (fuzzy `maxEdits: 1`): searching a contact name with exactly one typo — e.g. contact **"aprizal"** typed as **"arizal"**, **"aprizall"**, or **"abrizal"** — still returns the "aprizal" contact instead of an empty result. On **production (v2.satuinbox.com)** the same behavior does not work: those queries return no results. Ticket **#2969** (Global Search — add fuzzy/typo-tolerant matching) specifies that typo-tolerant matching with `maxEdits: 1` must work in Global Search. The behavior is present in the dev environment but absent in production, creating an environment inconsistency for the same feature. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Log in to **production** (`app.satuinbox.com`) as an Agent. 2. Open Global Search (sidenav **Cari** or `Ctrl+K` / `Cmd+K`). 3. Type `aprizal` (control) and confirm the contact appears in the result. 4. Clear the input, then type `arizal` (1-char typo — missing letter "p"). 5. Observe the result state. 6. Repeat step 4–5 with `aprizall` (extra letter "l") and `abrizal` (letter "p" → "b"). 7. Repeat steps 3–6 on **dev-v2** (`dev-v2.satuinbox.com`) with the same account and contact data. ## Actual Result * **Production**: typing `arizal`, `aprizall`, or `abrizal` returns **no results** (empty state) for the existing contact "aprizal". * **dev-v2**: the same three queries return the "aprizal" contact in the Global Search suggestion result. * Each typo is exactly **1 edit** away from "aprizal": `arizal` (delete "p"), `aprizall` (insert "l"), `abrizal` (substitute "p"→"b"). ## Expected Result * Per ticket **#2969**, Global Search MUST surface typo-tolerant matches within `maxEdits: 1` — `arizal`, `aprizall`, and `abrizal` should return the "aprizal" contact on **both** environments, ranked at the lowest (fuzzy) tier below exact/prefix/partial matches. * Production behavior should be consistent with dev-v2. ## Impact ## Evidence _Evidence slots left empty — attach the dev/prod comparison captures from testing._ ## Initial Observation * The 1-edit typo tolerance is functional on **dev-v2** (fuzzy `maxEdits: 1` behavior confirmed by the ticket's own example: `arizal` → `aprizal`). * The same queries return an empty result on **production**. * Both environments were tested with an Agent account searching the same existing contact name. ## Possible Root Cause _(Optional)_ Possible affected areas: * **Production deployment/rollout** — the #2969 fuzzy tier change (`SCORE_FUZZY` in `conversation-search.repository.ts` / `ticket-search.repository.ts`) may be deployed to dev-v2 only; the production backend build may not include the change yet. * **Feature flag / environment configuration** — the fuzzy clause may be gated by an environment-specific flag enabled on dev but not production. * **Backend code** — `conversation-search-atlas.pipeline.ts` / ticket-service equivalent (Atlas `$search` `should` clauses) and the `_scoreField > 0` guard. _Hypotheses only — deployment status needs engineering/PM confirmation._ ## Recommendation _(Optional)_ 1. Confirm with Engineering/PM whether ticket **#2969** is intended to be live on production and its current rollout status. 2. Compare the deployed backend version (search service) between dev-v2 and production to verify whether the fuzzy tier is included in the production build. 3. If the feature is intended for production, schedule the release; if rollout is not yet planned, confirm the expected go-live so QA can track it. ## Additional Notes * **Ticket reference**: `TestingSatuinbox/OpenProject/ticket/feature/2969-Global Search — add fuzzy:typo-tolerant matching (gap vs conversation-list search).md` — proposal specifying a new lowest-priority `SCORE_FUZZY` rung below `SCORE_PARTIAL` in both conversation and ticket search repositories. * `**maxEdits: 1**` **semantics** = exactly 1 edit (missing/extra/wrong letter, or adjacent swap). `arizal` / `aprizall` / `abrizal` are all 1 edit ✅; a 2-edit typo (e.g. `arizl`) correctly returns nothing — not part of this issue. * **PRD conflict**: Ticket #2969 **reverses FR-008** — a spec-level change. Flag for PM confirmation on rollout intent and PRD revision. * **Consistency reference**: the conversation-list (inbox) search already applies `fuzzy: {maxEdits: 1}` on `contactInfo.displayName` — Global Search on production is the only surface missing typo tolerance once dev is considered. * **Empty-state copy** (PRD): "Tidak ada data terkait ditemukan." * **Precondition for verification**: the "aprizal" contact must exist and be accessible to the Agent account in both environments.

allWorkPackages.subject: Broadcast - WAPI - broadcast wapi not follow broadcast hour
allWorkPackages.description:
step : * broadcast at 22:00 * set send now * broadcast show status scheduled
--- ## Investigation note (2026-09-15) — code-trace only, not reproduced **Hypothesis: the broadcast-hours shift is never resolved, because `isBroadcast` is `false`/absent on the company's shift documents.** ### Where the window is applied `apps/broadcast-service/src/app/processors/spin-text.processor.ts` - `handleEmitToScheduleBroadcast()` (L334-362) resolves one `shift` per batch via `getShiftForBatch()`. - `getShiftForBatch()` (L759-788) — when the batch has no `shiftId`, it falls back to: `listResponse?.items?.find((i) => i.isBroadcast)` (**L783**). - `getWorkingIntervalsForDay()` (L800-814): if `shift` is `undefined`, it silently falls back to the hardcoded window `BROADCAST_START_HOUR`..`BROADCAST_END_HOUR` = **06:00-21:00 GMT+7** (`apps/broadcast-service/src/app/constants/base.constant.ts` L61-63). - `enforceSchedulingWindow()` (L871-907) then pushes the emit time into the next valid interval. So a failed shift lookup does not error — it degrades to a hardcoded default. Nothing in the logs says "shift not found". ### Why `isBroadcast` is likely false 1. `isBroadcast` is declared `@Prop({ default: false, type: Boolean })` in `apps/company-service/src/app/schemas/shift.schema.ts` **L104-105**, and was introduced together with `DEFAULT_BROADCAST_HOURS` in commit `6ea8eaea` ("Fix/485 improve schedulling broadcast"). The proto field `optional bool isBroadcast = 9` (`proto/company.proto` L407) landed in the same commit. 2. `DEFAULT_BROADCAST_HOURS` (`apps/company-service/src/app/constants/default-broadcast-hours.constant.ts`) is only written at company registration, from `company.service.ts` L107-112. **Companies registered before `6ea8eaea` therefore have no shift document carrying `isBroadcast: true`** — the field defaults to `false` on every pre-existing shift. For those tenants `find((i) => i.isBroadcast)` returns `undefined` on every batch. 3. `isBroadcast` is an `optional` proto field. When it is `false` on the Mongo document, proto3 may omit it on the wire, so the broadcast-service consumer sees `undefined` — indistinguishable from "not a broadcast shift". ### Second, independent way the lookup can miss `ShiftService.buildShiftFilters()` (`apps/company-service/src/app/services/shift.service.ts` L179-186) hard-excludes `isDefault: { $ne: true }`, and `getShiftForBatch()` requests only `{ limit: 25, page: 1, sort: 'createdAt:desc' }` (spin-text.processor.ts L777). The broadcast-hours shift is created at registration time, so it is the **oldest** shift for the tenant. Any company with more than 25 shifts will never see it on page 1 — same silent fallback to 06:00-21:00. ### What to check on the affected tenant (no code change needed yet) ```js db.shifts.find( { companyId: ObjectId(""), organizationId: ObjectId("") }, { name: 1, isBroadcast: 1, isDefault: 1, timezone: 1, intervals: 1, createdAt: 1 } ) ``` Expect to find either no `Broadcast Hours` document at all, or one with `isBroadcast: false`/absent. ### Action Not fixing in this pass. **Please retry the broadcast** after confirming/repairing the shift document — if the tenant's `Broadcast Hours` shift exists with `isBroadcast: true` and the 22:00 send still reports `scheduled`, the cause is elsewhere and this note should be reopened with the new evidence. If the hypothesis holds, the durable fixes are (a) a backfill setting `isBroadcast: true` on the `Broadcast Hours` shift for tenants registered before `6ea8eaea`, and (b) making the fallback in `getShiftForBatch()` log a warning instead of failing open to the hardcoded window. _All findings above are traced from source; no reproduction environment was available, so the DB-level claims are inferred, not observed._

allWorkPackages.subject: Widget Domain Topic Filter
allWorkPackages.description:
# **PRD PATCH: Widget Domain-Based Topic Filter**

> **Type:** Patch / Addendum
> **Base PRD:** `PRD/Widget/PRD Widget.md` (v1.1)
> **Author:** Dany Christian
> **Date:** 2026-08-03
> **Updated:** 2026-08-12
> **Change Intake Brief:** `Assessments/widget/widget-domain-topic-filter/widget-domain-topic-filter-change-intake-brief.md` (v1.2)

---

## **Revision History**

| Version | Date | Author | Changes |
|---------|------|--------|--------|
| v1.3 | 2026-08-12 | Dany Christian | Align with brief v1.2: add `*.domain.com` wildcard support, hostname-only format (no protocol), www. auto-strip, IP literal exact-only, fail-open behavior, max 10 domains per topic, `matchDomain()` function spec, updated edge cases and test scenarios. |
| v1.2 | 2026-08-03 | Dany Christian | Patch: Add domain-based topic filter for widget accounts. Topics can now be restricted to specific website origins. |

---

## **1. Patch Summary**

| Item | Description |
|------|-------------|
| Purpose | Allow admin to restrict widget topics to specific website domains, so visitors on different websites see only relevant topics. |
| Scope | Add optional `allowedDomains` field to widget account topic config. Add `domain` param to widget topic fetch API. Add domain input to widget account create/edit form. Domain matching: exact hostname + `*.domain.com` prefix wildcard. |
| Non-Scope | Regex domain matching. Domain DNS validation. Per-page/per-path widget rules. Analytics on domain usage. Multi-level wildcard (`*.*.domain.com`). |

---

## **2. Problem Statement**

| ID | Problem | Impact |
|----|---------|-------|
| PS-PATCH-001 | Multi-brand / multi-site companies cannot restrict which topics appear on which website. All topics are shown on all sites. | Visitors see irrelevant topics, reducing chat entry quality and agent triage efficiency. |

---

## **3. User Stories and Acceptance Criteria**

| ID | Priority | User Story | Acceptance Criteria |
|----|----------|------------|---------------------|
| US-PATCH-001 | P0 | As an Admin, I want to set allowed domains per topic in a widget account so visitors on specific websites see only relevant topics. | 1. Given I am creating a widget account, When I select a topic and enter domain "toko-a.com", Then the topic is only visible when the widget loads on toko-a.com or www.toko-a.com. 2. Given I leave the domain field empty, When the widget loads on any website, Then the topic is visible everywhere (backward compatible). 3. Given I enter "toko-a.com, toko-b.com", When the widget loads on toko-a.com, Then the topic appears. 4. Given I enter `*.toko-a.com`, When the widget loads on shop.toko-a.com, Then the topic appears. |
| US-PATCH-002 | P0 | As a Visitor, I want to see only topics relevant to the website I'm on so I don't get confused by unrelated topics. | 1. Given I open the widget on toko-a.com, When the topic list loads, Then I see only topics where toko-a.com matches allowed domains OR topics with no domain restriction. 2. Given no topics match my domain and no unrestricted topics exist, When the topic list loads, Then I see no topic selector (form skips topic selection). |

---

## **4. Functional Requirements**

| Category | Requirements |
|----------|-------------|
| Data Model | FR-PATCH-001 [P0]: System MUST add optional `allowedDomains: string[]` field to WidgetTopicInfo in AccountChannel schema. Default value MUST be empty array `[]`. FR-PATCH-002 [P0]: System MUST NOT require `allowedDomains` — existing topics without this field MUST be treated as visible on all domains. |
| API | FR-PATCH-003 [P0]: `GET /account-channel/topics` (open API) MUST accept optional `domain` query parameter (hostname only, no protocol). FR-PATCH-004 [P0]: When `domain` param is provided, system MUST filter topics using `matchDomain()` function: exact hostname match + `*.domain.com` prefix wildcard + auto-strip `www.` prefix. FR-PATCH-005 [P0]: When `domain` param is omitted or empty, system MUST return all topics (fail-open). FR-PATCH-006 [P0]: Domain matching MUST be case-insensitive, hostname-only (no protocol/port/path). IP address literals MUST use exact match only (wildcard not applied). |
| Domain Matching | FR-PATCH-013 [P0]: `matchDomain(domain, patterns)` function MUST implement: (1) auto-strip `www.` prefix from both input and patterns, (2) `*.domain.com` matches bare `domain.com` and any `*.domain.com` subdomain, (3) IP address literal blocks wildcard pattern, (4) empty/missing patterns = match all (fail-open). FR-PATCH-014 [P0]: `allowedDomains` entries MUST be validated on save: max 10 entries per topic, no URL path/port/query chars (`/`, `:`, `?`, `#`), trimmed and lowercased. |
| Admin UI | FR-PATCH-007 [P0]: Widget account create/edit form MUST include a "Domain yang Diizinkan" input field per topic. FR-PATCH-008 [P1]: Domain input MUST accept comma-separated hostname values (e.g., "toko-a.com, *.toko-b.com"). FR-PATCH-009 [P1]: Domain input MUST be optional. Empty = all domains. Hint: "Kosongkan untuk menampilkan di semua website." |
| Widget Client | FR-PATCH-010 [P0]: Widget embed script (`apps/widget/helpers/scripts/chat-widget-setup.ts`) MUST pass `window.location.origin` as `origin` query parameter to the widget iframe URL. FR-PATCH-011 [P0]: Widget Next.js app MUST read `origin` from URL and extract hostname, then pass as `domain` param to topic fetch API call. |
| Backward Compat | FR-PATCH-012 [P0]: All existing widget accounts and topics MUST work without any migration. No breaking change. `allowedDomains: []` or missing field = visible on all domains. |

---

## **5. Domain Matching Specification**

### 5.1 `matchDomain()` Function

```typescript
/**
 * Match origin domain against allowedDomains patterns.
 * ponytail: string ops only, no regex for matching logic.
 * Upgrade to regex if pattern complexity grows beyond *.prefix.
 */
function matchDomain(domain: string, patterns: string[]): boolean {
  if (!patterns || patterns.length === 0) return true; // no restriction = all domains
  
  const d = domain.toLowerCase().replace(/^www\./, '');
  
  return patterns.some(p => {
    const pattern = p.toLowerCase().replace(/^www\./, '');
    
    // IP address literal: exact match only
    if (/^\d{1,3}(\.\d{1,3}){3}$/.test(d) || /^\d{1,3}(\.\d{1,3}){3}$/.test(pattern)) {
      return d === pattern;
    }
    
    // Wildcard prefix: *.domain.com
    if (pattern.startsWith('*.')) {
      const base = pattern.slice(2);
      return d === base || d.endsWith('.' + base);
    }
    
    // Exact match
    return d === pattern;
  });
}
```

### 5.2 Match Examples

| Pattern | Domain | Match? | Reason |
|---------|--------|--------|--------|
| `toko-a.com` | `toko-a.com` | ✅ | Exact match |
| `toko-a.com` | `www.toko-a.com` | ✅ | www. auto-stripped |
| `toko-a.com` | `api.toko-a.com` | ❌ | Exact, no wildcard prefix |
| `*.toko-a.com` | `api.toko-a.com` | ✅ | Wildcard subdomain match |
| `*.toko-a.com` | `toko-a.com` | ✅ | Wildcard includes bare domain |
| `*.toko-a.com` | `shop.id.toko-a.com` | ✅ | Ends-with match (1 level covers nested) |
| `192.168.1.1` | `192.168.1.1` | ✅ | IP exact match |
| `*.192.168.1.1` | `10.192.168.1.1` | ❌ | IP literal blocks wildcard |
| `localhost` | `localhost` | ✅ | Exact match |

### 5.3 Input Validation Rules

| Rule | Check | Error Message |
|------|-------|---------------|
| Max entries | `domains.length > 10` | "Maksimal 10 domain per topik" |
| No URL chars | contains `/`, `:`, `?`, `#` | "Domain tidak valid: hostname saja, tanpa protokol/port/path" |
| Trim + lowercase | auto on save | — |
| Empty string entries | skip/strip | — |

---

## **6. Edge Cases**

| ID | Scenario | Expected Behavior |
|----|----------|-------------------|
| EC-PATCH-001 | Widget loads on localhost (development) | Topic visible if "localhost" is in `allowedDomains`. Developer must add it explicitly. |
| EC-PATCH-002 | Widget loads on IP address | Exact match only. "192.168.1.1" matches ["192.168.1.1"]. Wildcard pattern on IP blocked. |
| EC-PATCH-003 | Admin enters domain with protocol "https://toko-a.com" | Validation rejects — `:` triggers URL char error. Hint guides to hostname-only format. |
| EC-PATCH-004 | All topics have domain restrictions, none match current domain | Widget shows no topic selector. Visitor can still start chat without topic (if conversation form allows). |
| EC-PATCH-005 | Topic A: `["toko-a.com"]`, Topic B: `[]` (all domains) | Both Topic A and Topic B appear on toko-a.com. Only Topic B appears on other domains. |
| EC-PATCH-006 | Admin edits topic domains while widget is already loaded | Changes apply on next widget page load (existing config caching behavior). |
| EC-PATCH-007 | `www.toko-a.com` in allowedDomains, visitor on `toko-a.com` | Match — www. auto-stripped on both sides. |
| EC-PATCH-008 | `*.toko-a.com` in allowedDomains, visitor on `toko-a.com` | Match — wildcard includes bare domain. |
| EC-PATCH-009 | No Origin/referer header (non-browser client, curl) | Fail-open — all topics returned. Domain filter ignored. This is display feature, not security. |
| EC-PATCH-010 | Admin enters 11 domains | Validation error: "Maksimal 10 domain per topik" |

---

## **7. Field & Validation**

| Field | Type | Example | Validation | Required | Default |
|-------|------|---------|------------|----------|--------|
| allowedDomains | string[] | `["toko-a.com", "*.toko-b.com"]` | Hostname only. Max 10. No `/`, `:`, `?`, `#`. Trimmed, lowercased on save. | No | `[]` |
| domain (query param) | string | `toko-a.com` | Hostname extracted from `window.location.origin`. URL-decoded. | No | undefined (fail-open: returns all topics) |

---

## **8. API / Event Contract**

| Contract | Method | Producer | Consumer | Request / Payload | Response / Ack | Compatibility Notes |
|----------|--------|----------|----------|-------------------|----------------|---------------------|
| GET /account-channel/topics | HTTP GET (open API) | API Gateway (`account-channel.open.controller.ts`) | Widget client (iframe) | `?domain=toko-a.com` (new optional param, hostname only) | `{ topics: [...], subtopics: [...] }` — filtered by domain via MongoDB `$elemMatch` | Backward compatible. No param = all topics. |
| gRPC: GetAccountChannelTopics | gRPC | API Gateway | Channel Service | `origin_domain: string` (new optional field in proto) | Filtered topic list | Proto3 backward compatible (empty = absent). |

---

## **9. UI & UX Requirements**

| Component | Description | UX Flow | Related User Story IDs |
|-----------|-------------|---------|------------------------|
| Widget Account Modal — Domain Input | New "Domain yang Diizinkan" chip/tag input below each topic select in create/edit widget account modal. | 1. User selects topic. 2. User optionally enters comma-separated hostnames. 3. User saves. | US-PATCH-001 |
| Domain Input Hint | Helper text: "Kosongkan untuk menampilkan di semua website. Gunakan *.domain.com untuk semua subdomain. Contoh: toko-a.com, *.toko-b.com" | — | US-PATCH-001 |
| Domain Input Validation Error | Inline error when >10 domains or invalid characters | — | US-PATCH-001 |
| Widget Topic Section — Empty State | When no topics match current domain, hide topic selector entirely. | — | US-PATCH-002 |

---

## **10. Non-Functional Requirements**

| Attribute | Target |
|-----------|--------|
| Performance | Topic filter MUST NOT add measurable latency. MongoDB `$elemMatch` on ~10-50 topics = <1ms. |
| Security | Domain param is display/tenant isolation, NOT a security boundary. Tenant scope remains enforced via `companyId` from API key auth. |
| Widget Package Size | Embed script change: +40 bytes (1 line). Total: ~19.6KB. Budget: 60KB. |
| Cache | `/widget/settings` cache (1 day TTL, per company) NOT affected. Topic list is separate aggregation endpoint. |

---

## **11. Dependencies & Risks**

| Type | Item | Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------|------|------------|
| Internal | Widget embed script change (FE monorepo: `apps/widget/helpers/scripts/chat-widget-setup.ts`) | Low risk — 1 line addition | Standard build + manual E2E verify |
| Internal | Aggregation pipeline change | Medium risk — wrong filter logic could hide all topics | Integration tests for all filter scenarios (11 test cases) |
| Internal | gRPC proto change | Low risk — additive field only | Proto3 backward compatible |
| Product | Admin UX — domain format confusion | Users may enter wrong format | UI hint with examples. Validation rejects URL-format input with clear error. |
| Product | Fail-open bypass concern | Non-browser clients can see all topics by not sending domain | Accepted — this is display feature, not security boundary. Document in limitations. |

---

## **12. Limitations**

| Limitation | Impact | Workaround |
|------------|--------|------------|
| 1-level wildcard only (`*.domain.com`) | `*.shop.domain.com` not supported as single pattern | List specific subdomains as separate entries (max 10 per topic) |
| No domain DNS validation | Admin can enter non-existent domains | UI hint, no backend enforcement |
| Fail-open when no domain | Domain restriction bypassable by non-browser clients | Accepted — display feature, not security boundary |
| Max 10 domains per topic | Large multi-brand companies may hit limit | Use wildcard patterns to reduce entries |
| Domain filter only on topic list fetch | Topics embedded in conversation config at account channel level | Already scoped correctly — topic is resolved at conversation start |

---

## **13. Appendix**

| Item | Notes |
|------|-------|
| References | Base PRD: `PRD/Widget/PRD Widget.md` v1.1, Brief: `Assessments/widget/widget-domain-topic-filter/widget-domain-topic-filter-change-intake-brief.md` (v1.2) |
| Related Future Consideration | PRD v1.1 Section 14 mentions "Per page widget rules: Show different widget account by URL path." This patch is a scoped subset — per-domain topic filtering. Path-level rules remain future. |
| Open Questions | None (all resolved in Change Intake Brief v1.2) |
| Embed Script Location | FE monorepo: `apps/widget/helpers/scripts/chat-widget-setup.ts` → compiled to `apps/widget/public/scripts/widget.min.js` |
| Prototype | `PRDanalisis/prototype/widget-domain-filter.html` — interactive admin + visitor preview

allWorkPackages.description: # TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT DOCUMENT (TRD) — Phase 1 **Feature**: SuperAdmin Global Company Access — **Phase 1: Company List/Search + Onboarding Approval** **Source PRD**: [`prd/prd-superadmin-global-access.md`](https://project.ordo.co.id/prd/prd-superadmin-global-access.md) (v1.0, 2026-06-22) — §5 US-001..004, §6 FR-001..014/FR-021/FR-028, §16 API rows 1–3, §17 rows 1–2, §20 Phase 1. **Engineering Lead**: Naftal Yunior **Status**: Draft for implementation hand-off **Date (Asia/Jakarta)**: 2026-07-01 ## 0\. Product intent (the three constraints) The user's framing, applied across all three phases: 1. **Frontend = a brand-new dedicated app** for the SuperAdmin surface (`frontend/apps/system`, domain `system.satuinbox.com`), a sibling to `omnichannel`/`widget`, reusing the shared `@satuinbox/*` packages. 2. **Backend = a dedicated API surface** used _only_ by that app: a new `/system/*` route group on `api-gateway` with **its own Swagger docs** at `/system/docs`, **separate** from the existing main API docs (`/docs`) and Open API docs (`/open-api/docs`). 3. **Reuse existing microservice logic** — the `/system` gateway routes call existing gRPC RPCs where they already exist (e.g. company approve/reject) and add narrowly-scoped new RPCs only where needed (e.g. company search). **No change to existing tenant runtime, existing controllers, or existing docs surfaces.** ## 1\. How this maps to the PRD (Phase 1 only) Phase 1 is a **read + narrow-write** feature: a new `/system` HTTP surface (SUPER\_ADMIN-guarded, own Swagger) that lists all companies with owner info, flags companies pending onboarding, and approves/rejects onboarding — reusing the company-service approve/reject lifecycle and adding only server-side search/filter + an audit trail. ## 2\. Current-state architecture (verified) ### 2.1 api-gateway is HTTP-only with a two-Swagger-surface pattern * `api-gateway` is the single REST entry point and a pure gRPC **client** (CLAUDE.md; `backend-architecture.md`). Never add a gRPC server to it. * **Two independent Swagger surfaces exist today**, both in [`apps/api-gateway/src/main.ts`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/api-gateway/src/main.ts) (~`:135-195`): * `setupSwagger()` (~`:135-168`) → main API at `/docs`, `SwaggerModule.createDocument(app, config, { include: [AppModule] })`. * `setupOpenApiSwagger()` (~`:174-195`) → Open API at `/open-api/docs`, `createDocument(app, openConfig, { include: [OpenApiModule] })`. * **Scoping mechanism (critical):** the `include: [Module]` option filters which controllers appear in each document. This is exactly the hook Phase 1 uses for a third surface. * Global prefix set in `configureGlobalPrefix()` (~`:92-97`): `app.setGlobalPrefix(apiPrefix, { exclude: ['health','metrics', \`${openApiPrefix}/(.\*)\`\] })`. Port from` API\_GATEWAY\_PORT `(default 3000, ~`:257-261`). Helmet + compression + CORS configured (~`:50-87\`). * gRPC clients: `GRPC_CLIENTS` array [`app.module.ts`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/api-gateway/src/app/app.module.ts) (~`:109-158`) includes `COMPANIES_PACKAGE_NAME`; registered via `ClientsModule.registerAsync` + `createGrpcClientFactory` (~`:265-278`). ### 2.2 Guards + role decorator for SUPER\_ADMIN already exist * `JwtAuthGuard` ([`guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/api-gateway/src/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts)) — attaches `request.user` after JWT validation; honors `@Public()`/`@SkipAuth()`. * `RolesGuard` ([`guards/roles.guard.ts`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/api-gateway/src/guards/roles.guard.ts) ~`:28-99`) — reads `@RequireRoles(RoleTypeEnum[])` metadata; extracts roles from `user.role ?? user.userContext?.permission?.role`; throws `ForbiddenException` if the required role is absent. * `AdminOnly()` decorator = `applyDecorators(RequireRoles(RoleTypeEnum.SUPER_ADMIN))` ([`libs/common/src/lib/decorators/index.ts:209`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/libs/common/src/lib/decorators/index.ts#L209)). **Reuse verbatim.** * `@RequestContext()` ([`decorators/index.ts` ~`:100-127`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/libs/common/src/lib/decorators/index.ts#L100)) → `{ correlationId, ipAddress, requestId, role, source, teams, tenant:{companyId,organizationId}, timestamp, user, userAgent }`. * `RoleTypeEnum.SUPER_ADMIN = 'SUPER_ADMIN'` ([`libs/common/src/lib/enums/index.ts:14-22`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/libs/common/src/lib/enums/index.ts#L14)); SUPER\_ADMIN default permissions include `ALL_ACCESS = '*'` ([`constants/default-permission.constant.ts:249-253`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/libs/common/src/lib/constants/default-permission.constant.ts#L249)). ### 2.3 company-service already lists all companies + approve/reject (reuse) * **List (unscoped) already exists:** `ListCompanies` RPC ([`proto/company.proto:10`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/proto/company.proto#L10)) → `getPaginatedCompanies()` ([`repositories/company.repository.ts:44`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/company-service/src/app/repositories/company.repository.ts#L44)) queries with an **empty filter** `**{}**` (~`:47`) → returns **all** companies. No tenant scoping at the repo — exactly what a platform admin needs. Request/response: `ListCompaniesRequest{ pagination, metadata }` / `ListCompaniesResponse{ items[], pagination }` (`company.proto` ~`:102-110`). * **Approve/Reject already exist:** `ApproveCompany` / `RejectCompany` RPCs ([`company.proto:11-12`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/proto/company.proto#L11)); services `approveCompany()` ([`services/company.service.ts:173`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/company-service/src/app/services/company.service.ts#L173)) and `rejectCompany()` (~`:192`). Approve sets `isVerified=true, approvedAt, approvedBy`; reject sets `rejectedAt, rejectedBy, rejectedReason` ([`company.repository.ts:66-102`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/company-service/src/app/repositories/company.repository.ts#L66)). Requests: `ApproveCompanyRequest{ companyId, userId, metadata }`, `RejectCompanyRequest{ companyId, reason, userId, metadata }` (`company.proto` ~`:188-199`). Emits `COMPANY_APPROVE`/`COMPANY_UPDATED` (approve) and `COMPANY_REJECTED` (reject) events ([`company.service.ts:389-409`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/company-service/src/app/services/company.service.ts#L389)). * **api-gateway already fronts these:** [`company/company.controller.ts`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/api-gateway/src/app/company/company.controller.ts) has `POST /company/register` (~`:84`), `POST /company/:id/approve` (~`:122`), `POST /company/:id/reject`. These live on the **main** docs surface and are (per current guards) not framed as a superadmin lane. **Phase 1 does not touch this controller** — it adds a parallel `/system` controller. * **Onboarding status is DERIVED, not an enum.** Company schema ([`schemas/company.schema.ts`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/company-service/src/app/schemas/company.schema.ts)): `isVerified` (~`:147`), `approvedAt/approvedBy` (~`:153-158`), `rejectedAt/rejectedBy/rejectedReason` (~`:161-171`), embedded `owner: OwnerInfo{ userId, fullName, email, phone, lastSyncedAt }` (~`:20-53`). Derivation: pending = `!isVerified && !approvedAt && !rejectedAt`; approved = `isVerified && approvedAt`; rejected = `rejectedAt` set. * **Owner is denormalized** on the company doc (`owner.fullName/email/phone`) — **no people-service gRPC hop needed** to render owner in the list (satisfies FR-005). * **One organization per company** at creation ([`schemas/organization.schema.ts`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/company-service/src/app/schemas/organization.schema.ts); created in `company.service.ts` ~`:87-93`). Relevant for Phase 2 impersonation target selection, not Phase 1. * **No search exists** — `getPaginatedCompanies` has no name/owner filter. This is the one net-new backend capability in Phase 1 (§6.2.2). ### 2.4 Frontend: apps are auto-discovered; clean scaffold recipe * Turbo discovers workspaces via `"apps/*"` glob (root [`frontend/package.json`](https://project.ordo.co.id/frontend/package.json) ~`:30-33`); [`frontend/turbo.json`](https://project.ordo.co.id/frontend/turbo.json) declares `globalEnv` (~`:3`) and the `dev/build/lint/check-types` pipeline. A new `apps/system` is picked up automatically once its `package.json` exists. * App skeleton (from `apps/omnichannel`): `package.json` (deps on `@satuinbox/{ui,helpers,i18n,react-query,constants,types,...}`, `next`, `next-intl`, `next-auth`), `next.config.ts` (next-intl plugin + `dotenv` loads root `../../.env` + `output:'standalone'`), `tsconfig.json` (extends `@satuinbox/typescript-config/nextjs.json`), `postcss.config.js` (delegates to `@satuinbox/tailwind-config/postcss`), `app/layout.tsx`, `app/[locale]/layout.tsx` (imports `@satuinbox/ui/styles.css`, validates locale via `hasLocale(intlRouting.locales, locale)` → `notFound()`), `providers/Providers.tsx` (`QueryProvider > NextIntlClientProvider > AuthSessionProvider`), `app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/authOption.ts`, `types/next-auth.d.ts`. * next-auth Credentials provider POSTs to `${NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/auth/login`, returns `{ id, email, fullName, accessToken, refreshToken, role:{code,name,permission[]}, company, organization, onboardingStatus }`; **role is readable at** `**session.user.role.code**` → `=== 'SUPER_ADMIN'` gates the app. * i18n: `@satuinbox/i18n` `routing.ts` locales `['en','id']`, `defaultLocale:'id'`; namespaced messages under `packages/i18n/src/translations//{en,id}.json`. ### 2.5 What does NOT exist yet (confirmed absent) * No `/system` route group, no `SystemModule`, no `/system/docs` Swagger surface. * No company **search** (name/owner) in company-service. * No `apps/system` frontend app. * No generic audit log or superadmin audit events (Phase 1b adds the audit foundation — see §6.3; full detail in [`trd-superadmin-phase-2-impersonation-readonly.md`](https://project.ordo.co.id/trd-superadmin-phase-2-impersonation-readonly.md) §6.4). ## 3\. Target architecture (Phase 1) ```text system.satuinbox.com api-gateway (HTTP :3000) ┌────────────────────┐ HTTPS ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ apps/system (NEW) │──────────►│ SystemModule (RouterModule path 'system')│ │ next-auth: role │ Bearer │ @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard, RolesGuard) │ │ === SUPER_ADMIN │ │ @AdminOnly() on every controller │ │ TanStack Query │ │ own Swagger surface /system/docs │ └────────────────────┘ └───────────────┬───────────────┬──────────┘ gRPC ListCompanies│ gRPC Approve/Reject│ emit audit event ▼ ▼ ▼ (RabbitMQ) ┌───────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────┐ │ company-service │ │ audit-service │ │ + search/filter/sort │ │ + superadmin log│ │ on ListCompanies │ │ schema+handler│ │ (existing approve/ │ └──────────────────┘ │ reject reused) │ └───────────────────────┘ own Mongo each ``` **Everything additive.** Existing controllers, docs surfaces, and tenant runtime are untouched (constraint 3, FR-028). ## 4\. Phasing overview (Phase 1 sub-phases) 1a/1b are backend and can proceed while 1c scaffolds the FE. 1d integrates. ## 5\. Cross-cutting decisions ## 6\. Detailed design by surface ### 6.1 Gateway `/system` surface (Sub-phase 1a) **6.1.1 Module.** New `apps/api-gateway/src/app/system/system.module.ts`. Imports `ConfigModule`; reuses the already-registered gRPC clients (import the same `ClientsModule` registration, or rely on the global `AppModule` client registration — pick whichever matches how other feature modules obtain clients; company/auth clients are registered at `app.module.ts` ~`:265-278`). Declares the `/system` controllers (1b adds `SystemCompanyController`; later phases add impersonation/quick-action controllers). **6.1.2 Routing prefix.** Mount under `/system` with Nest `RouterModule.register([{ module: SystemModule, path: 'system' }])` in `app.module.ts`, so controllers use `@Controller('companies')` and resolve at `/system/companies`. (Alternative: give each controller an explicit `@Controller('system/...')` prefix and skip `RouterModule` — pick one and be consistent; `RouterModule` is cleaner and keeps the Swagger `include` filter clean.) **6.1.3 Third Swagger surface (constraint 2).** In `main.ts`, add `setupSystemSwagger(app, configService)` mirroring `setupOpenApiSwagger` (~`:174-195`): * New `DocumentBuilder().setTitle('SatuInbox SuperAdmin Platform API').setDescription('Internal platform-admin endpoints — SUPER_ADMIN only').setVersion('1.0').addBearerAuth().build()`. * `SwaggerModule.createDocument(app, systemConfig, { include: [SystemModule] })` — **scopes the doc to SystemModule controllers only**, so `/system/docs` never leaks tenant endpoints and `/docs` never shows `/system` endpoints. * `SwaggerModule.setup(systemDocPrefix, app, () => document, { swaggerOptions: {...} })` with `systemDocPrefix` from a new config key `app.systemDocsPrefix` (default `'system/docs'`). * Add `\`${systemDocPrefix}/(.\*)\``(or`'system/docs'`) to the global-prefix` exclude `list (~`:94`) so the docs UI resolves outside` /api\`. * Add config keys to the api-gateway config factory: `SYSTEM_DOCS_PREFIX` (default `system/docs`). No secret. **6.1.4 Guards.** All `/system` controllers: `@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard, RolesGuard)` + `@AdminOnly()` (D3) + `@ApiBearerAuth()`. Never `@Public()`. **6.1.5 Done-when.** `npx nx build api-gateway` passes; `/system/docs` renders and lists only SystemModule controllers; `/docs` and `/open-api/docs` unchanged; a non-SUPER\_ADMIN token → `403` on any `/system/*` route. ### 6.2 Company list/search + approve/reject (Sub-phase 1b) **6.2.1 Proto changes** — [`proto/company.proto`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/proto/company.proto). Extend `ListCompaniesRequest` (backward-compatible, all optional): ```proto message ListCompaniesRequest { common.Pagination pagination = 1; optional common.MetaData metadata = 2; optional string search = 3; // matches name, owner.fullName, owner.email, _id optional string onboardingStatus = 4; // 'pending' | 'approved' | 'rejected' (derived filter) optional string sortBy = 5; // 'createdAt' | 'name' (default createdAt) optional string sortDir = 6; // 'asc' | 'desc' (default desc) } ``` `**pendingCount**` **is delivered via a separate count call (LOCKED)** — not a field on `ListCompaniesResponse`. Add a dedicated RPC `CountCompanies(CountCompaniesRequest) returns (CountCompaniesResponse{ count })`, where `CountCompaniesRequest{ optional string onboardingStatus, optional string search, optional common.MetaData metadata }` reuses the same filter builder as `ListCompanies` (so the FE can count pending, or any filtered subset, independently of the current page). This keeps the list response unchanged and lets the pending badge/count refresh without refetching the list. Then `cd backend && npm run generate-proto-types` (service `build` depends on `^generate-proto-types`). **6.2.2 company-service search/filter (net-new).** In [`company.repository.ts`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/company-service/src/app/repositories/company.repository.ts) `getPaginatedCompanies()` (~`:44`), replace the empty `{}` filter with a built `FilterQuery`: * `search` → `$or` regex (case-insensitive, escaped) over `name`, `owner.fullName`, `owner.email`; if the term is a valid ObjectId, also match `_id`. * `onboardingStatus` → translate to field predicates (D5): `pending` → `{ isVerified:false, approvedAt:{$in:[null,undefined]}, rejectedAt:{$in:[null,undefined]} }`; `approved` → `{ isVerified:true }`; `rejected` → `{ rejectedAt:{$ne:null} }`. * `sortBy/sortDir` → sort spec; default `{ createdAt:-1 }`. * Keep `paginate()`/`IPaginatedResponse` conventions. Add/confirm indexes: `name` already indexed (~`:116`); `owner.userId`/`owner.fullName` indexed (~`:22-34`); consider a `createdAt` index for the sort. Escape the regex term (reuse a common escape util). * Add a `countCompanies(filter)` method that runs `countDocuments()` over the **same built** `**FilterQuery**` (search + onboardingStatus), backing the new `CountCompanies` RPC. Factor the filter builder into a shared private helper so list and count never drift. **6.2.3 Gateway** `**SystemCompanyController**` — `apps/api-gateway/src/app/system/company/system-company.controller.ts` (in SystemModule): * `GET /system/companies` — query DTO `ListSystemCompaniesDto` (class-validator + `@ApiProperty`): `search?` (trim, ≤200), `onboardingStatus?` (enum), `page?`/`limit?` (defaults `DEFAULT_PAGE`/`DEFAULT_MIN_LIMIT_PAGINATION`), `sortBy?`/`sortDir?`. Calls `ListCompanies`; maps each item to `SystemCompanyListItemDto` with a **derived** `**onboardingStatus**` (D5) and owner fields — name/email in the list, phone reserved for detail (D6; owner-fields-shown confirmed). Returns the standard paginated envelope (`mapPaginatedResponse`); the list response does **not** carry a pending count. * `GET /system/companies/count` — query DTO `CountSystemCompaniesDto` (`onboardingStatus?`, `search?`); calls the new `CountCompanies` RPC; returns `{ count }`. The FE calls this with `onboardingStatus=pending` for the queue badge (FR-009), independently of the list page. * `GET /system/companies/:id` — calls existing `GetCompany` RPC; maps to `SystemCompanyDetailDto` (owner, timestamps, verification/rejection context — FR-013/014). * `POST /system/companies/:id/approve` — calls existing `ApproveCompany({ companyId, userId: reqCtx.user...id, metadata })` (D4/D7), passing `correlationId`/`ipAddress`/`userAgent` in `metadata` so company-service can emit the audit (§6.3, D8). Return `{ success:true }`. * `POST /system/companies/:id/reject` — body `{ reason }` (required, validated); calls `RejectCompany({ companyId, reason, userId, metadata })` with the same enriched `metadata`; **audit is emitted by company-service, not here**; return success. * Extract typed `CompanyServiceClient` in `onModuleInit()` (never the constructor) — match [`company.controller.ts:61-63`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/api-gateway/src/app/company/company.controller.ts#L61). * gRPC errors (e.g. already-resolved → conflict, not-found) surface through the existing `grpc-to-http-exception.filter` (D10). **6.2.4 Pending highlight (FR-008/009).** The derived `onboardingStatus === 'pending'` drives the per-row FE badge; the queue count comes from the separate `GET /system/companies/count?onboardingStatus=pending` call (D-pendingCount), not from the list payload. **6.2.5 Approve/reject reuse (FR-010..012).** No new lifecycle — the existing RPCs already set fields + emit `COMPANY_APPROVE`/`COMPANY_REJECTED`. The `/system` route is just a superadmin-guarded entry point. **6.2.6 Detail context (FR-013).** `GetCompany` already returns the full `Company` message (owner, verification/rejection fields, timestamps) — enough for the review drawer without a new RPC. ### 6.3 Audit foundation + approval/rejection audit (Sub-phase 1b) audit-service is write-only and event-driven today (only `OpenApiRequestLog`; consumes `@EventPattern(EventTypeEnum.OPEN_API_REQUEST_LOGGED)`; `saveLog` inserts via Mongoose — [`processors/open-api-log.processor.ts:23`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/audit-service/src/app/processors/open-api-log.processor.ts#L23), [`services/open-api-log.service.ts:23`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/audit-service/src/app/services/open-api-log.service.ts#L23)). `AuditActionEnum` exists ([`enums/index.ts:174-185`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/libs/common/src/lib/enums/index.ts#L174)). Producers emit via `clientAudit.emit(EventTypeEnum.X, payload)` ([`api-gateway/.../open-api-log.service.ts:30-38`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/api-gateway/src/open-api-log/open-api-log.service.ts#L30)). Phase 1 lays the **generic superadmin audit log** (also used by Phases 2 & 3): * **New schema** `apps/audit-service/src/app/schemas/superadmin-audit-log.schema.ts` (collection `superadmin_audit_logs`, `{ timestamps:true, versionKey:false }`): `actorUserId` (indexed ObjectId), `actorRole` (string), `action` (string, indexed — e.g. `superadmin_company_approved`), `targetType` (string, e.g. `company`), `targetCompanyId`/`targetOrganizationId` (ObjectId, indexed), `targetId` (string), `before` (Object, nullable), `after` (Object, nullable), `reason` (string, nullable), `correlationId` (string), `ipAddress`/`userAgent` (string), `metadata` (Object). No TTL (audit is long-lived, PRD §21 "long-term retention / immutable preferred"). * **New event constants** in `EventTypeEnum`: `SUPERADMIN_COMPANY_APPROVED = 'superadmin.company.approved'`, `SUPERADMIN_COMPANY_REJECTED = 'superadmin.company.rejected'` (Phases 2/3 add impersonation/write-mode values in their TRDs). * **New processor** `superadmin-audit-log.processor.ts` with `@EventPattern` handlers → `SuperadminAuditService.record(payload)` → insert. Fire-and-forget + error-absorb, matching `saveLog`. * **Producer (LOCKED: company-service).** `company-service` emits the audit event from inside `approveCompany()`/`rejectCompany()` — right where the lifecycle write commits — via an injected `ClientProxy` (`@Inject(ASYNC_SERVICE_PREFIX + AUDIT_PACKAGE_NAME)`), payload `{ actorUserId, actorRole:'SUPER_ADMIN', action, targetType:'company', targetCompanyId:id, reason?, correlationId, ipAddress, userAgent }`. Actor context is threaded in on the RPC: `Approve/RejectCompanyRequest` already carry `userId` + `metadata` (D7) — extend the `metadata` mapping in the gateway to also pass `correlationId`/`ipAddress`/`userAgent` from `@RequestContext()` so company-service has everything it needs. This guarantees the audit only fires when the DB write actually succeeded (no gateway/service divergence) and keeps the write on the async path. **Note:** this means the reused approve/reject services gain one additive emit — still no change to their lifecycle writes or existing `COMPANY_APPROVE`/`COMPANY_REJECTED` events (D4 preserved). * **Read API** (for the future superadmin audit view) is **out of Phase 1 scope** — added when Phase 2 needs the impersonation log view. Structure the schema now so the read RPC is a pure add later. ### 6.4 Frontend — new `apps/system` app + company UI (Sub-phases 1c, 1d) **6.4.1 Scaffold (1c).** Create `frontend/apps/system` as a sibling app (§2.4 recipe): * `package.json` `"name":"system"`, `dev`/`start` on **port 3003**, deps mirroring omnichannel (`@satuinbox/{ui,helpers,i18n,react-query,constants,types}`, `next`, `next-intl`, `next-auth`, `react`). * `next.config.ts` (next-intl plugin + dotenv root `.env` + `output:'standalone'`), `tsconfig.json`, `postcss.config.js`, `middleware.ts` (next-intl locale middleware, mirror omnichannel). * `app/layout.tsx` + `app/[locale]/layout.tsx` (import `@satuinbox/ui/styles.css`, `hasLocale` validation → `notFound()`, wrap in `Providers`, `ToastProvider`). * `providers/Providers.tsx` (`QueryProvider > NextIntlClientProvider > AuthSessionProvider`) + `AuthSessionProvider.tsx`. * next-auth `app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/authOption.ts` — Credentials provider posts to `**${NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/system/auth/login**` (the 2FA-verified login endpoint, §6.5), passing `{ identifier, password, code }`; **reject in** `**authorize**`**/**`**signIn**` **if** `**role.code !== 'SUPER_ADMIN'**` (D9); `types/next-auth.d.ts` augmented types. The 2-step email-code UI is built in Sub-phase 1f; 1c wires the provider + gating. * i18n: a new `system` namespace (or reuse) under `packages/i18n` for `en`+`id`; register in `messages.ts`. All copy via next-intl (ESLint bans hardcoded strings). * Base shell: minimal sidebar/topbar, `(auth)/login`, `(main)` group, `forbidden` page (EH-001). Route group under `app/[locale]/`. * **Env (LOCKED):** reuse the existing `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (the api-gateway origin) — the `/system/*` routes are on the same gateway and login is the shared `/auth/login`, so no new env var is added. The system API calls hit `${NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/system/...`. Add an axios instance (reuse `@satuinbox/helpers` `useAxiosPrivateApi` — it attaches the Bearer token + refresh) whose base path is `${NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/system`. **6.4.2 Company list + approval UI (1d)** under `app/[locale]/(main)/companies/`: * Thin `page.tsx` + `ManageCompaniesPage.tsx` (per repo page pattern). * Data hooks (TanStack Query, `useQueryWithSession`): `use-manage-system-company-api-request.ts` (wraps `useAxiosPrivateApi`, calls `GET /system/companies`, `GET /system/companies/:id`, `POST .../approve`, `POST .../reject`), `use-get-system-companies.ts` (query, keys from a new `SYSTEM_COMPANY_QUERY_KEY` const; debounced search 300ms; server-side pagination), `use-approve-company.ts`/`use-reject-company.ts` (mutations → invalidate list + toast on success/error via `showToast`). * Components (reuse `@satuinbox/ui` atoms/molecules): companies table (name, owner name/email, created date, onboarding status), **pending badge** (`Company baru` / `Menunggu approval` — CVA variant), pending-count header, search `Input`, status filter, pagination, `CompanyDetailDrawer` (owner + review context), approve/reject actions (reject requires a reason field; confirm dialog). Empty state (FR-002 search no-match) and error/retry state (EH-002). * Copy in `id` + `en` from the PRD §9 UI copy list (`Daftar Company`, `Company baru`, `Menunggu approval`, `Setujui onboarding`, `Tolak onboarding`). * EC-001/004: after approve/reject, invalidate + refetch so a concurrently-resolved row shows the up-to-date state; a `409` conflict shows a stable message + refetch. ### 6.5 SuperAdmin login email verification code — 2FA (Sub-phases 1e backend, 1f frontend) The superAdmin app login gains a mandatory second factor: after password validation, an **8-digit** code is emailed to the superAdmin and must be entered to obtain a platform-admin session. The code is valid 24h and **reused** (same code resent) if one already exists in-window (US-008, FR-031..036), and is **not invalidated on successful verify** — the compensating controls are verify-attempt rate-limiting + a resend cooldown (D11). This reuses existing transactional-email + cache infrastructure — no new email or storage stack. **Current-state reuse (verified):** * Transactional email is **auth-service → RabbitMQ → notification-service → AWS SES v2**. auth-service emits via `@Inject(ASYNC_SERVICE_PREFIX + NOTIFICATIONS_PACKAGE_NAME) ClientProxy` (e.g. `emitUserResetPasswordEvent` [`app.service.ts:890-902`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/auth-service/src/app/app.service.ts#L890)); notification-service consumes with `@EventPattern` ([`app.controller.ts:30-75`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/notification-service/src/app/app.controller.ts#L30)) → `SesService` (`SESv2Client` + `SendEmailCommand`, `MAIL_FROM` from `notification.mailFrom`, [`ses.service.ts:75-122`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/notification-service/src/app/ses.service.ts#L75)). Templates are Handlebars `.hbs` under `notification-service/src/assets/templates/` via `EmailTemplateService.compileTemplate()` ([`email-template.service.ts:13-43`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/notification-service/src/app/email-template.service.ts#L13)); names in `TEMPLATES` ([`constant/base.constant.ts:3-7`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/apps/notification-service/src/app/constant/base.constant.ts#L3)). * Short-lived storage: `@omnichannel-satuinbox-be/cache` `CacheService.set(key, value, ttlSeconds)/get/del/ttl` ([`cache/services/cache.service.ts:46-137`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/libs/cache/src/lib/services/cache.service.ts#L46)); `CacheTTLEnum.ONE_DAY = 86400` ([`cache.enum.ts:23-35`](https://project.ordo.co.id/backend/libs/cache/src/lib/enums/cache.enum.ts#L23)); prefixes in `CacheKeyPrefixEnum`. **No OTP precedent** — first numeric email code; prior verification used JWT link tokens in Mongo. **6.5.1 Backend (1e).** * **Proto** (`auth.proto`, `AuthService`): `RequestSuperAdminLoginCode(SuperAdminLoginRequest) returns (RequestCodeResponse{ sent, maskedEmail, expiresInSec, retryAfterSec })` and `SuperAdminLogin(SuperAdminLoginRequest) returns (LoginResponse)`, where `SuperAdminLoginRequest{ identifier, password, code (empty for the request step; 8 digits on verify), ipAddress, userAgent }`. `generate-proto-types`. * `**RequestSuperAdminLoginCode**`: validate credentials (existing local-credential check) + resolved role `SUPER_ADMIN` (on failure return a **generic** error — don't reveal which factor failed). **Abuse guard (LOCKED):** before generating/resending, enforce a **resend cooldown** and a **request rate limit** keyed by `{userId}`+`{ipAddress}` (Redis counter with TTL); if within cooldown, return `retryAfterSec` without re-sending. Then **generate-or-reuse**: `key = superadmin:login-code:{userId}` (add to `CacheKeyPrefixEnum`); if `CacheService.get(key)` returns a code, reuse it; else create an **8-digit** numeric code and `CacheService.set(key, { code, createdAt }, CacheTTLEnum.ONE_DAY)`. Emit `EventTypeEnum.SUPERADMIN_LOGIN_CODE` `{ email, code, fullName, lang }`. Return `{ sent:true, maskedEmail, expiresInSec: CacheService.ttl(key), retryAfterSec }`. * `**SuperAdminLogin**`: re-validate credentials + `SUPER_ADMIN` + verify the submitted **8-digit** `code` equals the cached code (constant-time compare). On success issue the normal `LoginResponse` (session + tokens). Per requirement the code is **not** deleted on success (lives its 24h, reused) — a same-day re-login uses the same code. **Verify-attempt rate-limiting (LOCKED, FR-036):** a per-key attempt counter in Redis locks the code for a cooldown after N failed verifies; reset on success. This is the security trade-off that lets the 24h reuse stand. * **notification-service**: new `@EventPattern(EventTypeEnum.SUPERADMIN_LOGIN_CODE)` → `SesService.sendSuperAdminLoginCodeEmail(email, code, fullName, lang)` using a new `TEMPLATES.SUPERADMIN_LOGIN_CODE = 'superadmin-login-code'` + `superadmin-login-code.hbs` (shows the code + 24h-validity notice; sender = `MAIL_FROM`). * **New event**: `EventTypeEnum.SUPERADMIN_LOGIN_CODE = 'superadmin.login.code'`. * **Gateway** `**/system**` **auth endpoints** (SystemModule; `@Public()`/`@SkipAuth()` — pre-auth — rate-limited; appear on `/system/docs`): `POST /system/auth/request-code` `{ identifier, password }` → `RequestSuperAdminLoginCode`; `POST /system/auth/login` `{ identifier, password, code }` → `SuperAdminLogin` → `LoginResponse`. The system app's next-auth Credentials provider posts to the latter (§6.4.1); it replaces the plain `/auth/login` for the system app. * **Audit (optional, reuse §6.3)**: emit `SUPERADMIN_LOGIN_SUCCEEDED`/`_FAILED` for traceability; never log the code value. **6.5.2 Frontend (1f).** system app `(auth)/login`: * **2-step**: step 1 — `identifier` + `password` → `POST /system/auth/request-code` (plain fetch/server action, not next-auth yet); on success show `Kode telah dikirim ke {maskedEmail}` + a countdown driven by `retryAfterSec`/`expiresInSec` + **Kirim ulang kode** (disabled until the resend cooldown elapses; resend → same code within window, EC-006). Step 2 — **8-digit** code input → `signIn('credentials', { identifier, password, code })`; the Credentials `authorize` posts to `POST /system/auth/login`, returns tokens, and still gates on `role.code === 'SUPER_ADMIN'` (§6.4.1, D9). Surface the verify rate-limit lockout as a distinct error state. * **States**: invalid/expired → EH-007 (`Kode verifikasi tidak valid atau kedaluwarsa`); email send failure → EH-008; resend cooldown to avoid email spam. * **Copy** id+en: `Masukkan kode verifikasi`, `Kode telah dikirim ke {email}`, `Kirim ulang kode`, `Kode verifikasi tidak valid atau kedaluwarsa`. ## 7\. Indexes, security, performance * **company-service indexes**: `name` (exists), `owner.fullName`/`owner.userId` (exist); add `createdAt` (sort) and confirm the search `$or` is index-supported enough for operational scale (PRD NFR ≤3s). Regex is anchored/escaped; unanchored `$or` regex won't use indexes efficiently — acceptable at current company counts, but note it (Limitation). If company count grows large, revisit Atlas Search (out of Phase 1 scope). * **Security**: server-side SUPER\_ADMIN enforcement on every `/system` route (D3/D9); the FE gate is defense-in-depth, not the control. `**/system/docs**` **MUST be protected in production (LOCKED, ops-owned):** gate the docs prefix behind basic auth (env-configured credential) or a network policy / ingress rule that restricts it to internal access — it must not be publicly reachable in prod even though it exposes only endpoint shapes, not data. Keep it open in local/dev. Track the chosen mechanism in the api-gateway deploy config. * **Privacy**: the list exposes only platform-admin-necessary owner fields (PRD §11 Privacy). No masking interceptor needed since SUPER\_ADMIN holds `VIEW_FULL_*` (§2.2), but do not add extra PII beyond owner name/email/phone. * **Observability**: emit `superadmin_company_list_fetch_total{actorId, resultCount}` and the audit events (PRD §22). Log correlationId on every `/system` request. ## 8\. Testing strategy Backend Jest `*.spec.ts` co-located, AAA, mock gRPC clients/repos; FE per `frontend-conventions.md`. Target ≥80% on new units. ## 9\. Acceptance traceability (PRD → verify) US-001 (list + owner + status + date) → §6.2.3/§6.4.2 · US-002 (search) → §6.2.2/§6.4.2 · US-003 (new-company highlight) → §6.2.4/§6.4.2 · US-004 (approve/reject) → §6.2.5 · FR-001..003 (SUPER\_ADMIN dedicated lane) → §6.1.4/D3 · FR-021 (audit) → §6.3 · FR-028 (no tenant side effects) → D1 · EH-001 (forbidden) → §6.4.1/D9 · EH-002 (list error) → §6.4.2 · EH-003/EC-001/EC-004 (approval conflict/concurrency) → D10/§6.4.2. ## 10\. Open questions (resolve before/within phase) * ~~FE app name/dir + dev port + domain~~ **LOCKED**: `frontend/apps/system`, port **3003**, domain `system.satuinbox.com`. * `~~/system~~` ~~base URL~~ **LOCKED**: reuse `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (same gateway host); system calls hit `${NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/system`. * ~~Confirm PRD "owner data fields shown"~~ **RESOLVED**: yes — owner fields are shown. Name/email in the list, phone in detail (§6.2.3, D6). * ~~Confirm~~ `~~pendingCount~~` ~~delivery~~ **RESOLVED**: **separate count call** — `GET /system/companies/count` backed by a new `CountCompanies` RPC; not a field on `ListCompaniesResponse` (§6.2.1/§6.2.3/§6.2.4). * ~~Confirm audit emit origin~~ **RESOLVED**: **company-service** emits, from inside `approveCompany()`/`rejectCompany()`; gateway threads actor context through the RPC `metadata` (D8, §6.3). * ~~Prod protection for~~ `~~/system/docs~~` **RESOLVED**: **yes, required in prod** — basic auth on the docs prefix or network/ingress restriction; open in dev (§7). * ~~Login-code security trade-off (§6.5)~~ **RESOLVED**: keep **24h reuse** + **verify-attempt rate-limiting** + **resend cooldown** (D11, §6.5.1). **Code length = 8 digits.** `request-code` gets an **abuse guard** (per-userId/IP rate limit + resend cooldown).
